children: The State Bank of India (SBI) has tightened its rules for Salary Package Account Holders. Starting October 1, the monthly limit for free transactions at other banks' ATMs and Automated Deposit cum Withdrawal Machines (ADWMs) will be cut from 10 to five. The new limit will apply regardless of the city or location.

The five-transaction limit covers both financial and non-financial activities, including cash withdrawals, balance enquiries and other banking services, with all transactions counted under the same pool.
This means a salary account holder who makes eight transactions at other banks' ATMs in a month will be charged for the last three transactions from October.

One thing, however, remains unchanged: SBI has not increased its per-transaction charges. Once the free limit is exhausted, cash withdrawals will cost Rs 23 plus GST per transaction, while non-financial transactions will attract a charge of Rs 11 plus GST.
While the charges remain unchanged, customers may find themselves reaching the free transaction limit much sooner than before.
Transactions at SBI's own ATMs will continue to be unlimited and free for salary account holders, as will cardless cash withdrawals at SBI and other bank machines.

If you are a salary account holder who regularly uses other banks' ATMs, keep track of your monthly transaction count from October 1 and consider shifting routine withdrawals to SBI ATMs to avoid additional charges.

title: SBI ATM rule change from October 1: Free transactions for salary accounts cut by half; check details
